content: Dame Betty Kershaw, DBE, FRCN, CStJ, currently holds the position of Professor of Nursing and serves as the Dean at the School of Nursing and Midwifery at the University of Sheffield. Previously, she was the Head of the Manchester College of Midwifery and Nursing and also served as the Director of Nursing Education at Stockport, Tameside, and Glossop College of Nursing. In 1995, she was awarded an honorary doctorate by Manchester University in recognition of her significant contributions to nursing education. In 1998, she was appointed Dame Commander of the Order of the British Empire (DBE) for her services to nursing education. Her recent international consultancy work includes projects in Colombia and China, focusing on the modernization of nursing practices. She is actively involved in the Department of Health Leadership Project, where she provides guidance on the development of leadership programs for black nurses to prepare them for leadership roles. Dame Betty Kershaw is a Fellow of the Royal College of Nursing and has previously served as its President. Additionally, she held the position of Chief Nursing and Social Care Officer for St John Ambulance. She resides in Manchester and is married to Sir Ian Kershaw, a distinguished historian.
